prompting.youReason: I prompt everything and give as much context as I can. Only effective with Claude due to file uploads.
prompting.swingPoint: Prompting everything is evidence of dependency not skill. 3pts for iteration instinct.
prompting.summary: Wk 1: 97% verdict (AI was 100%). Prompting everything is evidence of dependency not skill.
prompting.shove: Pick one prompt you sent this week — rewrite it with a clearer constraint and more context, then compare the two outputs side by side.

framing.youReason: I grab errors and paste them. I know to zoom out and get more details before randomly changing something.
framing.swingPoint: Knows the principle, paste-to-Claude is still the first reflex.
framing.summary: Wk 1: 94% verdict (AI was 100%). Knows the principle, paste reflex confirmed.
framing.shove: Next time something breaks, write one sentence describing the problem before you open Claude. Just one sentence.

creative.youReason: Structure and organization are all mine. AI proposed the visual language but I curated it and know when something looks wrong.
creative.swingPoint: Information architecture is yours. Visual execution language was AI-proposed — curation not origination.
creative.summary: Wk 1: 72% verdict (AI was 100%). Architecture yours. Visual language AI-proposed.
creative.shove: Next time you reject a Claude output, write down in 5 words why it looked wrong. That's your taste talking.

writing.youReason: I can express ideas raw — my journal entries prove it. I come short on technical implementation writing.
writing.swingPoint: Journal framework (floating, melting, tasking) is strong raw evidence. Technical writing still handed off.
writing.summary: Wk 1: 78% verdict (AI was 100%). Journal framework strong. Technical writing handed off.
writing.shove: Write a 3-sentence explanation of what a DFA is — no AI, no notes. Raw, imperfect, yours.

research.youReason: LLM first because it's faster but I know it's unreliable. I use a scratchpad to plan learning. I sort by question type — web for facts, AI for logic.
research.swingPoint: Scratchpad habit and question-type sorting earned points. LLM-first reflex confirmed by own words.
research.summary: Wk 1: 68% verdict (AI was 100%). Scratchpad real. LLM-first reflex confirmed.
research.shove: Pick one function you use this week and open the actual docs before asking Claude anything about it.

systems.youReason: I have the mental layout and describe it to Claude. I form my own metaphors and use AI to confirm not structure. I write until I hit a wall then search.
systems.swingPoint: Two real modes identified. Mode 1 is genuine systems thinking. Mode 2 is the default when confidence drops.
systems.summary: Wk 1: 75% verdict (AI was 100%). Two modes — Mode 1 genuine, Mode 2 dependent.
systems.shove: Next new problem — spend 5 minutes drawing boxes and arrows on paper before opening Claude. Any problem counts.

html.youReason: I cannot write a component at all. I only know basic C++ and barely Python.
html.swingPoint: Can't build it solo. 3pts for knowing what a component is.
html.summary: Wk 1: 97% verdict (AI was 100%). Can't build solo.
html.shove: Open a blank file right now and write a nav bar in HTML from memory. Don't open Claude until you've written 10 lines.

codelogic.youReason: I can guess what code points to but I don't know how often I'd be right. Pattern recognition but not line-by-line tracing.
codelogic.swingPoint: Pattern recognition is above zero. Guessing is not owning.
codelogic.summary: Wk 1: 90% verdict (AI was 100%). Pattern recognition real. Guessing not owning.
codelogic.shove: Take the next Claude-generated block, close the chat, and explain out loud what each line does. Record where you get stuck.

debugging.youReason: I know error types — ghost, runtime, compiled, style. But I can't fix them myself at all.
debugging.swingPoint: Error taxonomy from exposure is real. Can't fix alone confirmed.
debugging.summary: Wk 1: 93% verdict (AI was 100%). Error taxonomy real. Can't fix alone.
debugging.shove: Next time something breaks, give yourself 10 minutes before pasting. Read the error. Name the type. One hypothesis.

docs.youReason: Never actual docs. Always LLM first. I have been wrong a lot especially with ChatGPT.
docs.swingPoint: Own words: never go to primary sources. Wrong a lot as a result.
docs.summary: Wk 1: 97% verdict (AI was 100%). Never primary sources.
docs.shove: Open cppreference or MDN once today — look up any function you've used recently. Just read the signature and parameters.

testing.youReason: I never write tests. I am the mailman — I ask Claude for diagnostics and guide the zoom in and out.
testing.swingPoint: Directing the process is worth 5pts. Never writes tests confirmed.
testing.summary: Wk 1: 95% verdict (AI was 100%). Mailman. Never writes tests.
testing.shove: After the next Claude-generated function, write one edge case test yourself before running anything.

dsa.youReason: Maybe just theory. Cannot trace or implement cold at all.
dsa.swingPoint: Theory only. Exam room has no Claude.
dsa.shove: Trace a BFS on paper using a 5-node graph you draw yourself. No AI, no notes. Just you and the graph.

automata.youReason: I know DFA, NFA, GNFA, regular languages, sets. I can draw a DFA. But give me a language and I'm guessing. Concatenation and proofs — not there.
automata.swingPoint: Knows the landscape and can draw a DFA. Solving from spec cold is not there.
automata.summary: Wk 1: 85% verdict (AI was 100%). Can draw DFA. Solving from spec cold not there.
automata.shove: Draw a DFA that accepts strings ending in '01' — from scratch, no help. Check it after.

linalg.youReason: I know basic operations but got lost in row reduction running out of moves. No geometric intuition yet.
linalg.swingPoint: Basic operations real. Lost mid row-reduction means no geometric foundation yet.
linalg.summary: Wk 1: 88% verdict (AI was 100%). Basic ops real. Lost in row reduction.
linalg.shove: Do one row reduction problem by hand from your textbook. Write out every step. Find where you run out of moves.

calc.youReason: Took precalc, calc 1, calc 2. I know derivatives and integrals but need a refresher.
calc.swingPoint: Three completed courses is the strongest credential today. Refresher need keeps it at 68.
calc.summary: Wk 1: 68% verdict (AI was 100%). Three completed courses. Refresher needed.
calc.shove: Solve 3 derivatives cold from a practice sheet — no calculator, no AI. Check after.

stats.youReason: I reverse engineered it. Formula heavy. I don't feel like I learned anything. Barely passed.
stats.swingPoint: Reverse engineering formulas without understanding why — exactly what this axis measures against.
stats.summary: Wk 1: 95% verdict (AI was 100%). Reverse engineered. Didn't learn it.
stats.shove: Pick one stats formula you used in that class and explain in one sentence why it works, not just what it does.

discrete.youReason: I know propositions and logic decently. Proofs okay but need work on rigorous ones. Sucked at asymptotic and algo problems. Know combperm but need review.
discrete.swingPoint: Real pockets of knowledge in logic and propositions. Rigorous proofs and asymptotic are the exam gaps.
discrete.summary: Wk 1: 78% verdict (AI was 100%). Logic solid. Rigorous proofs and asymptotic are the gaps.
discrete.shove: Write a proof by induction for n >= 1: 1+2+...+n = n(n+1)/2. Cold. No help. Check after.
